# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates a complete, four-step pipeline to automate
**HydroLight radiative transfer simulations**. The workflow handles
everything from processing raw inherent optical properties (IOPs) to
executing the compiled batch models directly from the R console.

### Workflow Overview

- **Step 1**: Format raw absorption and attenuation data into
  HydroLight-standard AC files.
- **Step 2**: Compile and clean cruise hydrographic metadata.
- **Step 3**: Generate dynamic template-driven HydroLight configuration
  input scripts (`IFILEs`).
- **Step 4**: Execute the backend HydroLight terminal executable via an
  R subprocess.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 1: Formatting IOP Spectra

HydroLight simulations require depth-resolved inherent optical
properties (IOPs) in a strict text format. The
`create_hydrolight_ac_files()` function reads separate absorption (`a`)
and attenuation (`c`) CSV datasets, joins them by station/depth,
extracts the explicit wavelengths from the column metadata, and builds
formatted text matrices containing HydroLight headers.

### Function Definition

```{r step1-fun}

#Getting data
setwd("Q:/hydrolite_data/Explore_hydrolight/AC_corrected_datasets")

#read absorptions and attenuation

abs_dat<- read.csv("Atl_wat_all_depths_abs_spect_smoothed_2015.csv")
atts_dat<- read.csv("Atl_wat_all_depths_atts_spect_smoothed_2015.csv")

#full data
data_file<- read.csv("Q:/SCM-UC/Arctic-SCMs/final_fulldata.csv")
#filter year and longitudes 

data_file_2015_WSC<- subset(data_file,data_file$Longitude..degrees_east.>0 & 
                              data_file$year == 2015)
        #data_file$Latitude..degrees_north.>78.5 & data_file$Latitude..degrees_north.<79)
#Greenland stations
WSC_station<- unique(data_file_2015_WSC$Station)


#filter absorptions by stations
abs_dat_WSC<- abs_dat[ abs_dat$station %in% WSC_station,]

#filter attenuation by stations
atts_dat_WSC<- atts_dat[atts_dat$station %in% WSC_station,]



```

```{r include=TRUE}
create_hydrolight_ac_files(
  data_dir = "Q:/hydrolite_data/Explore_hydrolight/AC_corrected_datasets",
  output_dir = "Q:/hydrolight_runs/WSC_2015_bb_runs/ac_files",
  abs_file = abs_dat_WSC,
  atts_file = atts_dat_WSC,
  data_suffix = "_smooac_2015.txt",
  stations = NULL,
  max_depths = 50
)
```




### Create hydrolight Metadata

```{r}

meta_parameters<- c("X", "Cruise", "Station", "Type", "yyyy.mm.ddThh.mm.ss.sss",
                    "Longitude..degrees_east.", "Latitude..degrees_north.", "St.", "Depth..m.",
                    "Temperature...C.", "Salinity", "SigmT","PSDslope")
# Keep the data you considered as mets, for comparison and statistics
meta <- data_file_2015_WSC[, meta_parameters] 
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Extract year
# ---------------------------------------------------------
library(stringr)
meta$years <- str_split(meta$yyyy.mm.ddThh.mm.ss.sss, "-", simplify = TRUE)[,1]
# Unique stations
stations <- unique(meta$Station)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Convert to datetime
# ---------------------------------------------------------
meta$Time <- as.POSIXct(
  meta$yyyy.mm.ddThh.mm.ss.sss,
  format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M",
  tz = "UTC"
)
library(lubridate)
# Extract Hour (HH.MM format like Python)
meta$Hour <- format(meta$Time, "%H.%M")
# Day of year
meta$day <- yday(meta$Time)
#filter meta with greenaland 

#Tomorrow
meta_fil<- meta[ meta$Station %in% EG_station,]

# Final dataset
hydrometa_data <- meta_fil
# create bb_yung fraction

```

# create jungs fraction

```{r}
# 1. Prepare the data
df <- data.frame(
  index = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
  of = c(1.021, 1.040, 1.080, 1.175, 1.150),
  Junge.slope = c(3.0742, 3.2010, 3.4830, 4.0650, 4.8740),
  backscatter = c(1e-04, 1e-03, 1e-02, 1e-01, 4e-01)
)

# 2. Fit GAM: backscatter as target variable (Y), Junge.slope as predictor (X)
library(mgcv)
gam_model <- gam(backscatter ~ s(Junge.slope, k = 3), data = df)

# 3. Predict fitted values across a sequence of Junge.slope values for plotting
junge_seq <- seq(min(df$Junge.slope), max(df$Junge.slope), length.out = 200)
pred <- predict(gam_model, newdata = data.frame(Junge.slope = junge_seq))

# 4. Plot observed points and smooth curve (Linear Scale, No SD/SE lines)
plot(df$Junge.slope, df$backscatter, pch = 19, col = "blue",
     xlab = "Junge Slope", ylab = "Backscatter",
     main = "GAM Fit: Backscatter vs Junge Slope")
lines(junge_seq, pred, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# --- PREDICTION ON NEW HYDROMETA DATA ---

# 1. Extract PSD slope values
slope_vals <-data.frame( Junge.slope = Mod(hydrometa_data$PSDslope))

# 2. Create data frame with column name matching predictor 'Junge.slope'
#data_jung$Junge.slope <- data.frame(Junge.slope = slope_vals)

# 3. Predict backscatter from Junge slope
hydrometa_data$bb_yung <- predict(gam_model, newdata = slope_vals)


```

# Step 3: Generating HydroLight Configs (IFILEs)

The `hydrolight_ifile()` tool binds your compiled spatial/temporal
environmental metadata (`hydrometa_data`) directly into a template
HydroLight base model config. It handles string formatting rules
required by the engine core (such as conversion to decimal-comma arrays)
and cross-references the matching input tracks built in Step 1.

```{r}

for(i in WSC_station){

try(
hydrolight_ifile(
  station_name=i,
    hydrometa_data=hydrometa_data,
    template_path = "Q:/hydrolite_data/optical_proxyies_inverse/template_config.txt",
    working_dir = "C:/HE60/run/batch",
    ac_txt_dir = "Q:/hydrolight_runs/WSC_2015_bb_runs/ac_files",
    chl_txt_dir = "Q:/hydrolight_runs/WSC_2015_bb_runs/chl_a",
    chl_suffix = "_chlzdata.txt",
    cdom_txt_dir = "Q:/hydrolight_runs/WSC_2015_bb_runs/cdom_a",
    cdom_suffix = "_cdomdata.txt",
    data_suffix = "_smooac_2015.txt",
    bb_suffix = "_smooac_2015_Hydrolight_bb.txt",
    bb_txt_dir = "Q:/hydrolight_runs/WSC_2015_bb_runs/bb_outputs_0.020"
))

}

```

## Run in Hydrolight with pushbullet

```{r, knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "~C:/HE60/run/batch")}

library(progress)
library(stringr)
library(RPushbullet)

#----------------------------------------
# Pushbullet setup
#----------------------------------------
pbSetup(apikey ="o.fMNaBrPojmldEtyTVULaNN1OpBY6DfV7")

setwd("C:/HE60/run/batch/")
files <- list.files()

stations <- str_replace_all(files, c("^I" = "", "\\.txt$" = ""))

pb <- progress_bar$new(
  format = "Running [:bar] :current/:total (:percent) ETA: :eta",
  total = length(stations),
  clear = FALSE,
  width = 60
)

failed <- data.frame(
  station = character(),
  error = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (i in stations) {

  tryCatch(
    {
      run_hydrolight(station = i,model = "Eco")
    },
    error = function(e) {
      failed <<- rbind(
        failed,
        data.frame(
          station = i,
          error = conditionMessage(e),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      )
    }
  )

  pb$tick()
}

#----------------------------------------
# Summary
#----------------------------------------
successful <- length(stations) - nrow(failed)

cat("\n\nBatch processing finished.\n")
cat("Successful:", successful, "\n")
cat("Failed:", nrow(failed), "\n")

if (nrow(failed) > 0) {

  cat("\nFailed stations:\n")
  print(failed)

  report_file <- file.path(getwd(), "HydroLight_failed_report.csv")

  write.csv(
    failed,
    report_file,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  cat("\nReport saved as 'HydroLight_failed_report.csv'\n")

  # Pushbullet notification
  pbPost(
    type = "note",
    title = "HydroLight batch completed",
    body = paste(
      "Stations completed:", successful,
      "\nFailed:", nrow(failed),
      "\nReport:", report_file
    )
  )

} else {

  # Pushbullet notification
  pbPost(
    type = "note",
    title = "HydroLight batch completed",
    body = paste(
      successful,
      "stations completed successfully."
    )
  )

}




```
